# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first portrait browser game called **Chosen Spell Trials**. Preserve a one-requester-at-a-time reaction loop: a student enters, requests one of three spells, waits on a visible patience timer, and the player taps one of three bottom spell buttons. Correct taps add one House Point, play success feedback, and spawn the next student. Wrong taps shake the scene and reduce the current patience timer. If patience reaches zero, show a game-over report with final House Points and a restart button.

Theme the experience as a cozy gothic wizard-school adventure inspired by Harry Potter-style school fantasy without using licensed character names. The focal identity is a chosen first-year spellcaster mastering class trials with house identity, friendship stakes, castle scenes, magical particles, and responsive portrait UI.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a portrait-friendly canvas reaction/service game. One requester enters, waits, and displays one of three requested items. The player chooses among three bottom buttons. Correct input increments score and spawns a new requester; wrong input shakes the scene and subtracts patience; timeout ends the run; restart resets state.

## Protected mechanics
- One active requester at a time.
- Three mutually exclusive bottom touch/click choices.
- Random requested type per requester.
- Correct choice: +1 score, happy exit, particle feedback, next requester.
- Wrong choice: no score, shake/negative feedback, patience penalty of 500ms.
- Patience starts near 3000ms and decreases with score, clamped to 1000ms.
- Timeout triggers game over and restart flow.

## Rebuilt target
Chosen Spell Trials reinterprets the service loop as a wizard-school spell mastery class: classmates request Lumos, Wingardium, or Protego; the chosen student taps matching spell sigils; House Points replace score; the patience charm replaces waiting time.

## Runtime architecture
A new self-contained `index.html` uses inline CSS, inline JS, Canvas rendering, DOM HUD/overlays, Google Fonts from the approved catalog, and WebAudio oscillator tones for gesture-safe lightweight feedback.
